key_insight: Multi-omics and machine learning identified JAK–STAT signaling as a convergent immune signature of checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis, with amplified inflammatory programs in CHIP carriers.
clinical_relevance: These findings nominate cytokine-guided risk stratification and JAK–STAT-directed immunosuppression for future testing, rather than establish clinical benefit.
method: Machine learning and explainable AI analyzed cytokine profiles from patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors.
Single-cell multi-omics mapped immune-cell contributions and inflammatory pathways across three cohorts.
Stanford CyTOF data provided validation of Yale proteomic analyses.
evidence_signal: The study enrolled 236 cardio-oncology patients, including 88 receiving checkpoint inhibitors, and analyzed single-cell cohorts from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63).
watch_item: The abstract reports associations but no prospective predictive performance or treatment efficacy, so clinical implementation requires further validation.
paper_title: Cytokine Signatures of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis and the Modifying Role of Clonal Hematopoiesis: A Machine-Learning and Multi-Omics Study
